summary: Rizatriptan is an oral 5-HT1B/1D receptor agonist (triptan) for the acute treatment of migraine with or without aura in adults and children 6-17 years. The usual adult dose is 5 mg or 10 mg, repeatable after at least 2 hours, with a maximum of 30 mg in 24 hours. It is not for migraine prevention and is contraindicated in ischaemic heart disease, uncontrolled hypertension, recent ergot/triptan use and within 2 weeks of an MAO inhibitor. Patients taking propranolol should use the 5 mg dose (max 15 mg/24 h). It is available as conventional tablets and orally disintegrating tablets (MLT) that contain phenylalanine.

moa: Rizatriptan binds with high affinity to human 5-HT1B and 5-HT1D receptors. Activation of 5-HT1B receptors on intracranial blood vessels (including arteriovenous anastomoses) produces vasoconstriction, correlating with relief of migraine. Activation of 5-HT1D receptors on trigeminal sensory nerve endings inhibits release of pro-inflammatory neuropeptides (such as CGRP) and reduces transmission of nociceptive signals, thereby aborting the migraine attack.

preg: There are limited human data. Animal studies showed developmental effects only at maternally toxic doses. Use during pregnancy only if the potential benefit justifies the potential risk to the fetus.
lact: Rizatriptan is excreted in the milk of lactating rats; it is not known whether it is excreted in human milk. Exercise caution and consider avoiding breastfeeding for a period after dosing.
renal: No dose adjustment is specifically established, but plasma clearance is reduced in renal impairment (including haemodialysis patients). Use with caution and consider lower exposure to the drug.
hepatic: Plasma concentrations are increased in hepatic impairment. Use with caution in mild-to-moderate impairment; it has not been studied and should generally be avoided in severe hepatic impairment.

major: MAO-A inhibitors - markedly increase rizatriptan exposure; contraindicated during and within 2 weeks of MAOI use
Ergotamine, ergot-type drugs and other 5-HT1 agonists - additive vasospasm; do not use within 24 hours
Propranolol - increases rizatriptan exposure; use 5 mg dose (max 15 mg/24 h)
moderate: SSRIs / SNRIs - risk of serotonin syndrome
Other serotonergic agents - additive serotonergic effects
minor: No significant interaction with other beta-blockers (nadolol, metoprolol) at studied doses

missed: Rizatriptan is taken as needed for an acute migraine attack, not on a fixed schedule, so there is no missed dose. Take it when a migraine starts, and do not exceed the maximum daily dose.
overdose: Overdose may cause dizziness, somnolence, hypertension, syncope, vomiting and bradycardia. There is no specific antidote; provide supportive care, monitor for at least 12 hours or while symptoms persist, and manage cardiovascular effects. Haemodialysis is unlikely to be of benefit.
